key_insight: Reasoning-Trace Analysis makes LLM-generated Q-matrix assignments inspectable, revealing disagreements that matrix-level agreement and fit alone cannot explain.
engineering_relevance: AI-assisted assessment pipelines can use attribute-labeled reasoning traces to audit item–skill mappings alongside expert review and empirical validation.
method: Prompt LLMs to produce attribute-labeled solution steps.
Reconstruct Q-matrices from those steps and compare them with reference and directly generated matrices.
Inspect disagreements in item coding, labeling rules, and operation-level steps.
evidence_signal: A simulation and an empirical study with 11 fraction-subtraction items, 536 examinees, four LLMs, up to three temperatures, and 100 replications per condition found mean reference overlap of .809 for trace-derived matrices versus .877 for directly generated matrices.
watch_item: Trace-derived matrices varied more across replications; inspectable reasoning should supplement, not replace, expert review and response-data validation.
paper_title: Reasoning-Trace Analysis Using Large Language Models for Interpretable Q-Matrix Construction
